source_refs.note: Topic 22.1 with Quick Check 22.1, answered (PDF 89-90). The book also calls R an 'aryl' group, but -OH on an aryl ring is a phenol (22.5). The answers depend on reading the printed skeletal drawings and need review.

blocks.text: The hydroxyl group (-OH) is the functional group of all alcohols, which have the general formula ROH, where R is an alkyl group. The family also includes familiar substances such as cholesterol and the carbohydrates. Methanol (CH3OH) and ethanol (CH3CH2OH) are the first two members of the homologous series of monohydric alcohols.

items: By the number of -OH groups: monohydric alcohols have one (ethanol, propan-1-ol); polyhydric alcohols have more than one, e.g. ethane-1,2-diol (glycol, two) and propane-1,2,3-triol (glycerol, three).

blocks.alt: Four alcohols: ethanol CH3CH2OH and propan-1-ol CH3CH2CH2OH; 1,2-ethanediol (glycol), two CH2-OH units stacked; and 1,2,3-propanetriol (glycerol), CH2-OH, CH-OH and CH2-OH stacked.
blocks.caption: Monohydric and polyhydric alcohols: ethanol, propan-1-ol, glycol and glycerol (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 89).

items: By the carbon carrying -OH: in a primary (1) alcohol, RCH2OH, it is joined to one other carbon; in a secondary (2) alcohol, R2CHOH, to two; in a tertiary (3) alcohol, R3COH, to three.

blocks.alt: Three general displayed structures, each a carbon with R1 on the left and OH on the right: Primary alcohol (H above and below), Secondary alcohol (R2 above, H below) and Tertiary alcohol (R2 above, R3 below).
blocks.caption: General structures of primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 90).
